notes.body: California's Proposition 103 requires the Insurance Commissioner to review and approve auto-insurance rate changes before they take effect — unlike file-and-use states.
notes.title: Proposition 103 — rates need approval first

notes.body: Premiums must be based primarily on three factors, in this order: your driving safety record, how many miles you drive each year, and your years of driving experience.
notes.title: What sets your rate (in order)

notes.body: If you've been licensed 3+ years with a clean record (no more than one moving violation, no at-fault injury accidents, no DUI in 7 years), insurers must offer you a Good Driver Discount policy at least 20% below the rate you'd otherwise pay.
notes.title: 20% Good Driver Discount

notes.body: California bans credit-based insurance scores in auto rating, and ZIP code can't be used as the primary rating factor.
notes.title: What's not used in your rate

sources: CA Legislative Analyst's Office — Proposition 103 background
Consumer Watchdog — Proposition 103 & 20% Good Driver Discount
